title: A Case of the Mondays: I Told You So
_todo: BEN: paragraph 5 is the sentimental bit about Dad and Josh. I took a first pass so there's something to push against, but it's yours to rewrite. Everything else is checked against sources. Approve with: npm run monday:approve 2026-09-28
paragraphs: I told you so. I want to be gracious about this. I want to be the kind of man who wins quietly and says something about how it's a long season and there's a lot of football left. I am not going to be that man today. On Sunday morning, before the sun came up, I wrote that by pure mojo, by force of will, by whatever it is three related men can generate in a stadium on a Sunday afternoon, we were going to take this game, and that the reigning Super Bowl champions could file a complaint. Final score: Washington 33, Seattle 31. File your complaint.

The day started with a headlamp. I ran in the dark, came back, and my dad pulled up around 6:45 with the sun barely over the treeline. We pointed the car at Keswick to collect my brother Josh, and by then the back was packed to the roof with tailgate equipment in a way that suggested none of us had any idea what we actually needed. Somewhere in there I consumed a quantity of Red Bull and coffee that I would estimate at twelve million, which is to say I had manufactured legal cocaine in my own bloodstream. If you are old enough to remember Cornholio, I was that guy. I was him for about four hours.

The forecast said rain in Landover and we did not believe a word of it, because the sunrise on the way up was genuinely beautiful and it is hard to take a weather app seriously when the sky looks like that. Then I took a wrong turn, entirely my own doing, and we treated ourselves to a scenic drive-by of downtown DC before finding the interstate again. And then, of course, the rain came. Not a downpour, which you could at least respect. The other kind. The mist that isn't heavy enough to justify doing anything about it and soaks you anyway over ninety minutes. Apart from my navigational contribution, smooth sailing.

We parked in the Red Lot, which if you know, you know. Then came the tent. Twelve feet by twelve feet, brand new, never before assembled, versus three grown men and YouTube University. We got there eventually. We later learned that one of Josh's friends is an actual NASA engineer who arrived roughly ten minutes after we finished, which is the funniest possible timing and I will be thinking about it for a while. The reward was a food truck plate lunch, teriyaki chicken and mac salad, plus a smoked queso my brother made that I am still thinking about. We put away something in the neighborhood of four pounds of meat and cheese in forty-five minutes. Shout out to Josh and his whole crew, who broke that tent down in record time so we could actually get inside for kickoff.

And here's the thing underneath all of it. My dad is the reason I care about this team at all. Every bit of this traces back to him, and I don't get to say that to him in those words very often, because we're not really built that way. But there's a version of saying it that involves standing in a wet parking lot in Landover at nine in the morning arguing about tent poles, and eating too much queso, and getting into the building together. We do this once a year. It should be more. I know it should be more. Josh, Dad: same time next year, and let's not make it only next year.

Now, the part I've been chewing on. I have been to see every single team in the NFC East play. Every one. I have taken abuse in Philadelphia, which is practically a municipal service there, and I have given as good as I got in Dallas and New York and had a great time doing it. I have never experienced anything like the Seahawks fans on Sunday. It started in the lot, with a guy hanging out of a car window screaming profanity at us, and the line he landed on was "sorry about your quarterback." Jayden dislocated his elbow. The man is hurt. That's where you went.

It kept going inside. The guy directly in front of me applauded when a Commander went down injured. Applauded. I watched multiple Seattle fans yell at Commanders fans who were just walking up and down the steps, minding their own business, and I want to be precise here because I don't think every person who owns a Seahawks jersey is like this and I'm sure plenty of them were perfectly normal: this was not banter. Banter is fun. Banter is the whole point. This was aggressive and stupid and aimed at people who hadn't said a word. It's a football game. You can be better than that, and most fanbases manage it. Meanwhile everybody around us in burgundy was absolutely feral in the best possible way, which is exactly what a home opener in the rain should feel like.

As for the actual football, Marcus Mariota was magnificent and I will not be hearing otherwise. Our backup quarterback walked into a home opener against the reigning champions and beat them. The defense held Seattle to 44 rushing yards and forced three turnovers, and Washington turned those into 20 points, which the record books say we had not done since Week 17 of the 2005 season. Sonny Styles, three games into his NFL career and wearing the green dot, was everywhere. Kain Medrano came in off the bench and took one to the house in the fourth quarter. Dan Quinn got the better of the team he used to coach for. Quinn handed out game balls to Medrano and Mariota afterward, and nobody in that building needed convincing.

Mariota sealed it himself, which is the part I keep replaying. Third and seven, 1:15 on the clock, and he just ran for nine. No heroics required, no prayer downfield, just a 32-year-old journeyman putting his head down and ending the argument. I said before the game that I'd decided I liked him. I'd like to upgrade that.

Elsewhere: the subreddit spent Sunday evening throwing what it formally titled a "COWBOYS LOSE UPVOTE PARTY," and I have no further comment except that Victory Monday hits differently when the whole division cooperates. Virginia was idle this weekend after taking Delaware to the woodshed, and they're at Florida State on Saturday, which for reasons I will get into another time is a game with some history for me. And Jon Bernthal, who I had on decent authority would be in the building, was not in the building. Turns out we didn't need him. His presence would still have been appreciated.

So: 1-2, a backup quarterback who just beat the champs, a rookie linebacker who looks like a problem for the rest of the league, and a weekend in a parking lot with my dad and my brother. I told you so. Hail.
